---
title: "Boundary vintages"
jupyter: coi-docs
---

County and tract boundaries change: counties split, merge, or get replaced
entirely. A FIPS code without a vintage is an assembly name without a patch
level — the same code can mean a different shape depending on when it was
issued.

## The worked example: SVI's own county count

CDC/ATSDR's Social Vulnerability Index republishes the whole country every
edition, so its county count across editions is a direct, queryable record
of every boundary change that mattered at the county level between 2014 and
2022:

```{python}
#| echo: false
import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("INSTALL iceberg; LOAD iceberg; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;")
con.execute(
    "ATTACH 'canceronice' AS coi (TYPE ICEBERG, "
    "ENDPOINT 'https://icegate-canceronice.seandavi.workers.dev', "
    "AUTHORIZATION_TYPE 'none');"
)
con.sql("""
    SELECT svi_edition, count(distinct fips) AS counties
    FROM coi.raw.svi__county
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""").df()
```

3,142 / 3,142 / 3,142 / 3,143 / 3,144 — flat for three editions, then +1,
then +1 again. Both jumps are real redistrictings, not data errors, and both
are queryable directly:

```{python}
#| echo: false
con.sql("""
    SELECT svi_edition, count(*) AS rows
    FROM coi.raw.svi__county
    WHERE fips IN ('02261', '02063', '02066')  -- Valdez-Cordova / Chugach / Copper River
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""").df()
```

Alaska's Valdez-Cordova Census Area (`02261`) splits into Chugach (`02063`)
and Copper River (`02066`) starting with the 2020 edition — one row becomes
two, the +1 between the 2018 and 2020 counts.

```{python}
#| echo: false
con.sql("""
    SELECT svi_edition, count(*) AS rows
    FROM coi.raw.svi__county
    WHERE fips LIKE '09%'  -- Connecticut
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""").df()
```

Connecticut's eight legacy counties persist through the 2020 edition; the
nine 2022-vintage planning regions arrive with the 2022 edition — the +1
between the 2020 and 2022 counts.

The third real change in this window — South Dakota's Shannon County
becoming Oglala Lakota County in 2015 — is a rename-and-recode, not a
boundary change, so it doesn't move the county *count* at all; it shows up
instead as `fips` changing from `46113` to `46102` starting with the 2016
edition, with the pre-2016 code still resolving through `geography.alias`:

```{python}
#| echo: false
con.sql("""
    SELECT old_geo_id, new_geo_id, effective_year, change_type, old_name, new_name
    FROM coi.geography.alias
    WHERE old_geo_id = 'county:46113'
""").df()
```

## Why `geography.unit` carries a `vintage` at all

Every fact in the lake joins through `geography.unit` by `geo_id`, but a
`geo_id` alone doesn't say which boundary edition it belongs to. `vintage`
makes that explicit, and it's why every recipe on this site names a vintage
on its geography join (`u.vintage = 2026`) instead of trusting a measure's
own `geo_vintage` column — see [Time axes](time-axes.qmd) and
[cancer-on-ice#21](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-on-ice/issues/21) for
the open question that makes this necessary today. `geography.alias`
resolves an old code that was renamed or recoded (not reshaped) to its
current one, so a join on a retired code still finds its record instead of
silently dropping it.
